items.followUp: State Hooke's law and explain what happens when the elastic limit is exceeded.

rubric.why: Hooke's law describes the proportional relationship between force and extension, subject to the elastic-limit condition.
rubric.description: States that extension is directly proportional to the applied force up to the elastic limit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the proportional relationship and its condition.

rubric.why: The elastic limit is the greatest force up to which the body recovers its original shape after the force is removed.
rubric.description: Defines the elastic limit as the maximum force up to which a body regains its original shape when the force is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of the elastic limit.

modelAnswer: Hooke's law states that extension is directly proportional to the applied force, provided the elastic limit is not exceeded.
The elastic limit is the maximum force up to which a body regains its original shape when the force is removed.

items.followUp: Suggest two ways to reduce energy use in a school building.

rubric.why: Turning off unused devices avoids unnecessary energy consumption.
rubric.description: Suggests switching off lights or electrical appliances when they are not in use.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable measure that avoids unnecessary energy use.

rubric.why: Efficient devices and using daylight reduce the energy needed in a house.
rubric.description: Suggests using energy-efficient bulbs or appliances, or making use of natural light.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one additional suitable energy-conservation measure.

modelAnswer: Switch off lights and electrical appliances when they are not in use.
Use energy-efficient bulbs and appliances, and make use of daylight where possible.
